scenarios.context: A customer talks to the pharmacist.

speakerA.en: Good morning. How can I help you?
How long have you had it?
Take one of these tablets twice a day, after meals.
No, you don't. It's sixteen dollars.

speakerB.en: I have a headache and I feel tired.
Thank you. Do I need a prescription?

speakerA.en: I have a bad cough and a sore throat.
A little. My temperature is thirty-seven point eight.
How often do I take it?

speakerB.en: Try this syrup. Drink a lot of water and rest.
Three times a day. If you don't feel better in three days, see a doctor.

speakerA.en: Hello, I'm here to pick up my prescription.
Is it OK to take it with food?

speakerB.en: Can I have your name, please?
Here it is. Take one pill every morning.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, my eyes are red and I sneeze a lot.
Then I'll take one in the evening.

speakerB.en: It could be an allergy. Do you take any other medicine?
These allergy tablets can help. They may make you sleepy.
Good idea. Don't drive after taking one.

scenarios.context: A customer has a minor injury.

speakerA.en: I cut my finger in the kitchen.
Should I put some cream on it?

speakerB.en: Let me see. It isn't deep. I'll clean it first.
Yes, and change it every day.
Yes, this cream will help. Keep it clean and dry.
